records.name: Mile End Park
records.location: Mile End Park, Grove Road/Burdett Road and Regent's Canal, Tower Hamlets, east London E3.
records.description: Tower Hamlets Council describes an extensive multi-part linear park next to the Regent's Canal. Splashd claims anonymous cruising in an unspecified subarea but no current observed visit or precise mapped place is established.
records.original_source_description: This is a cruisy park, which is good in the fall and winter, when things grow out. It's also better here at night. The cruising area has been hacked down, so it's no longer safe to cruise in the main part of the park. It could grow back though.

records.name: Garfield Park - Merton
records.location: Garfield Recreation Ground, Garfield Road, Wimbledon/Merton SW19 8SJ; adjacent Wandle meadow requires separate identification.
records.description: The official Merton play-area directory confirms Garfield Recreation Ground and a fenced children's play area. Splashd suggests the park and adjoining meadow as a cruising location, but the alleged spot and recent activity are not corroborated.
records.original_source_description: There is Garfield Park and the Wandle Nature Meadow. They are joined by a small foot bridge, which is behind the school. Cruisiest spot, there is a big tunnel slide in the play area. Meet near there and then head off to the nature reserve.

records.name: Kennington Park
records.location: Kennington Park, Kennington Park Road, Lambeth, London SE11 4BE.
records.description: Lambeth verifies the public park and its opening hours, normally 07:30 until 15 minutes before sunset. Splashd's old mention of toilets and garden paths is uncorroborated by any post-cutoff eyewitness.
records.original_source_description: Cottage in the north side of the park by daytime. Around the garden in the south side of the park by nighttime. There are two cubicles in the toilet, and it is very small so difficult to hide anything, also really easy to tell if anyone is interested.

records.name: Victoria Park - Tower Hamlets
records.location: Victoria Park, east London, Tower Hamlets, E3/E9.
records.description: Victoria Park is a managed recreation area with specific gate hours. Tower Hamlets says gates normally operate from 07:00 until dusk; Splashd lists several unverified historical subareas but no precise verified current encounter.
records.original_source_description: There are three cruising areas in the park: "The Nature Trail"; bushes in south-west corner of park. "The Glade"; quiet area with two benches at the back, leading to a small woodland area. "The English Garden"; pretty garden next to deer pen.

records.name: Dickens Square Park
records.location: Dickens Square Park, Falmouth Road, Southwark, London SE1.
records.description: Splashd's London archive describes a small residential park bordered by several housing estates, alleging outdoor encounters without dates. No independent site-specific account, exact viable coordinates or recent firsthand activity could be confirmed.
records.original_source_description: Dickens Square is a small local park situated off Falmouth Road, SE1. It is located close the Rockingham and Lawson estates, and Trinity Newington estate, It's a smaller park with many hidden corners for actions. Go after dinner when the sun is setting.
